questions.question: What is the GAN training objective written as a minimax game?
options: min_G max_D  E_real[log D(x)] + E_fake[log(1 - D(G(z)))]
min_G min_D  ||x - G(z)||^2
max_G max_D  log D(x) + log D(G(z))
min_G max_D  KL[p_data || p_G]
questions.explanation: The minimax objective has the discriminator D maximizing its ability to tell real from fake, and the generator G minimizing the discriminator's advantage. At equilibrium, D outputs 0.5 everywhere and G matches the data distribution.

questions.question: Why is the non-saturating generator loss -log D(G(z)) preferred over the original log(1 - D(G(z)))?
options: It is easier to compute and requires no logarithms
The original loss saturates when D is confident, giving G near-zero gradient; the non-saturating form blows up in that regime, providing a strong signal
The original loss is unbounded from above, causing training instability
The non-saturating loss allows G to be trained more steps than D per iteration
questions.explanation: When D correctly classifies fakes with high confidence, log(1-D(G(z))) approaches 0 and gradients vanish. -log D(G(z)) has the opposite behavior: it grows large when D is confident, giving G a strong learning signal even early in training.

questions.question: What is mode collapse in GAN training?
options: The discriminator's loss collapses to zero and training stops
The generator produces a narrow range of nearly identical outputs despite diverse training data
Both networks converge to the Nash equilibrium simultaneously
The learning rate decays too fast, freezing both networks
questions.explanation: Mode collapse occurs when the generator finds a small set of outputs that fool the discriminator and exploits them repeatedly, failing to cover the full data distribution. One mode of the real data is never generated.

questions.question: Which GAN innovation replaced binary cross-entropy with the Wasserstein distance and a gradient penalty to fix vanishing gradients?
options: Progressive GAN
DCGAN
WGAN-GP
StyleGAN
questions.explanation: WGAN-GP (Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty) replaced the BCE discriminator loss with Earth-Mover distance and used a gradient penalty instead of weight clipping to enforce the Lipschitz constraint on the discriminator, providing smoother gradient flow to the generator.

questions.question: According to the lesson, what is the primary remaining advantage of GAN inference over diffusion models in 2026?
options: GANs produce higher visual quality than diffusion on open-domain prompts
GANs support text conditioning more naturally than diffusion
GANs generate a sample in one forward pass with no iterative steps, giving the lowest possible inference latency
GANs require fewer training samples than diffusion models
questions.explanation: A GAN generates samples with a single G(z) forward pass. No KV-cache, no schedule, no scheduler. StyleGAN3 generates a 1024x1024 face in under 10ms on a 4090, roughly 300x faster than a 50-step SDXL pipeline at the same resolution.

questions.question: Which technique introduced in 2018 constrains the discriminator's weight norms to stabilize GAN training and is still used in 2026 discriminators?
options: Batch normalization
Dropout
Spectral normalization
Layer normalization
questions.explanation: Spectral normalization (Miyato et al., 2018) constrains the discriminator's Lipschitz constant by dividing each weight matrix by its largest singular value, stabilizing training without the hyperparameter sensitivity of weight clipping.
